content.text:
I fixed the nested-link bug in `src/Tokenizer.ts`. I haven't run the tests because the folder has no `node_modules`, so the fix is verified by reading the code only.

**Cause:** `outputLink` (around line 16) sets `lexer.state.inLink` to `true` while it parses a link's text. When that text contains an image, the image's own `outputLink` call ran the same code and then set `inLink` to `false` on the way out. That cleared the flag the enclosing link had set. The text after the image, ` www.example.com`, was then no longer protected, so the GFM URL tokenizer turned it into a nested link.

**Fix:** `outputLink` now saves the previous `inLink` value and restores it when it finishes, instead of forcing it to `false`. A nested image no longer clears the enclosing link's state. The same restore path covers the case where a non-image link is rejected because it contains a link.

The bare-URL, email and reference-link cases in the report go through the same `outputLink` path or the same `inLink` check, so they should be covered by this change too. I haven't confirmed the output against the exact expected HTML in the report.
